commands.name: dev
commands.summary: Start interactive Brand Book dev server with HMR

commands.name: build
commands.summary: Build static brand book site and compiled design tokens

commands.name: tokens
commands.summary: Compile design tokens only (theme.css, tokens.ts, tokens.json)

commands.name: check
commands.summary: Check tokens: aliases, types, usage rules, contrast pairs, duplicates and review flags

commands.name: mcp
commands.summary: Set up blazon-mcp, the MCP server for coding agents: --print-config prints what registers it in a client, --check tests that it works; neither writes a file

commands.name: drift
commands.summary: Find tokens that have drifted from the live site: compare each token that names a source.cssVar with a page (http or https address) or a CSS file

commands.name: approvals
commands.summary: List the tokens and assets marked review ok with the fingerprint of their value today, to record in review.value so `blazon check` sees a later change

commands.name: plugin
commands.summary: Plugins: `check <program>` checks that a program follows the plugin protocol, `pin <path>` prints the digest that pins it, `profile` prints the profile blazon enforces

commands.name: explain
commands.summary: Explain a finding code: its severity, what it means, the fix and where to read more; with no code, list every code

commands.name: pin
commands.summary: Pin the blazon you build with: write blazon.lock with the commit of the blazon that runs this, so check, tokens and build refuse any other

commands.name: init
commands.summary: Scaffold a new Blazon brand book and design token structure

commands.name: preview
commands.summary: Preview the static production brand book build

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Check this machine and folder: Node version, brand folder, plugin folder safety, Chrome (if a plugin needs it) and blazon.lock; writes nothing

commands.name: get
commands.summary: Read one token: its value, type, CSS variable name in theme.css, its usage, pairs and logo rules, and the file it is in. To find a path, use blazon list

commands.name: list
commands.summary: List the tokens: path, type and value, and the token each aliases. With a group path, only the tokens in that group

commands.name: rules
commands.summary: Read the usage, pairs and logo rules of a token or a group, or of the whole brand when no path is given

commands.name: can
commands.summary: Ask whether the foreground token may be text (or, with --role ui, a border or focus ring) on the background token, by the brand rules; exits 0 allowed, 1 denied, 2 unknown token. Several pairs: --pair fg:bg, repeated

commands.name: contrast
commands.summary: Measure the contrast of the foreground token on the background token, optionally with a translucent token blended over the background; a measurement, not a verdict (exit 0; 2 when it cannot be measured)

commands.name: fonts
commands.summary: Read the fonts the brand loads (stylesheets and font files) and the families its tokens name

commands.name: logo
commands.summary: Read the configured logo variants and the rules each logo sidecar states: clear space, minimum size, lockups, ink

commands.name: brand
commands.summary: Print the brand as brand.json holds it, compiled now and written nowhere; --key prints one part

mcpTools.name: check_brand
mcpTools.title: Check the brand
mcpTools.description: Runs blazon check on the brand, without plugins, and returns its findings and counts. Plugins in blazon.json do not run, so the counts can be lower than `blazon check` prints, but only for a plugin with a check role; a build-only plugin adds no finding. `pluginsSkipped` and `warnings` list every configured plugin, since a role is known only by starting the plugin; `rulesNotRun` gives the code pattern of each (`name/*`). `byRule` groups the findings by code with a count and one example each. `passed` is false when the brand's own data has errors (`brandHasErrors`), and values read from such a brand can be wrong; a `pin-mismatch` finding is listed and counted but does not make `passed` false, and is also in `pinMismatch`. Returns at most `limit` findings (default 50, at most 500); `counts` stay whole. Not for reading a value: use get_token.

mcpTools.name: list_tokens
mcpTools.title: List the tokens
mcpTools.description: Lists the design tokens of the brand, or of one group, type or tier, each with its path, type, tier and value, in the order the token files write them. Use it to find a path or to read many values at once. `tier` (primitive, semantic or component) keeps to one layer of the brand. `theme` gives the values as that theme resolves them, and `defaultValue` on a token the theme changes; `themes` names the themes the brand has. For a token's CSS variable names and rules use get_token; for the brand's usage rules use get_rules. An answer over 40000 characters is cut to whole tokens, and `tokensTotal` says how many matched: narrow with `group`, `type` or `tier`.

mcpTools.name: get_token
mcpTools.title: Read a token
mcpTools.description: Looks up one design token of the brand: its value, type, the CSS variable names it gets, and the rules that apply to it. Use it for the value of a path you know; a group path is refused. With `theme` the value is the one that theme resolves, and `defaultValue` is the default one when it differs. For a path you do not know use list_tokens.

mcpTools.name: get_rules
mcpTools.title: Read the brand rules
mcpTools.description: Lists the brand rules (allowed uses, approved color pairs, logo restrictions) of a token or a group of tokens, or of the whole brand when no path is given. The whole brand can be larger than the size limit (40000 characters): give a path, or read the resource blazon://rules, which is not cut.

mcpTools.name: can_use
mcpTools.title: Can this color be used here
mcpTools.description: Answers whether one color token may be text on another color token, by the brand rules. Give `fg` and `bg` for one pair, or `pairs` (at most 50) for several in one call: the answer then has one result per pair, in order, and `allowed` is true only when every pair is. Exactly one of the two forms. Set `role` to ui for a focus ring, border or icon stroke: it is judged against the 3:1 non-text contrast and the pairs rules do not apply. `verbose` false leaves out the `checks` of an allowed answer; a denial keeps them. Contrast is measured as `check_brand` measures it: a color with an alpha channel is blended over its background, and `alpha` sets the foreground's opacity. The usage rules are read first, so a token a rule forbids is a denial even when it is not a color. A background with an alpha channel is an error, because what is behind it is not known, and so is a token that is not a color when usage allows it. A denied answer is a normal result (`allowed` is false, `reason` names the rule), not an error. Pairs come only from the `pairs` rules of token groups; component tokens are not read for them. For a color you have not picked, find one with list_tokens and type color.

mcpTools.name: measure_contrast
mcpTools.title: Measure the contrast of a color
mcpTools.description: Measures the contrast of one color token on another, optionally with one translucent color token blended over the background first. It is a measurement of what would be rendered, not a verdict: the answer has no `allowed` and does not say whether the brand approves; only `can_use` says whether the brand allows a pair, and a blend is never a listed pair. Use it for a tint or glow that no token names: give the opaque base `bg`, the tinting token as `with` and its opacity as `withAlpha`. `alpha` is the foreground's own opacity and `withAlpha` is the opacity of `with` over `bg`; they are different. `with` and `withAlpha` come together or not at all. The answer is `ratio` (WCAG 2.x), `level`, `nonText` (true from 3:1), `seen` (the two colors after blending, as hex) and `brandPairs`: the pairs the brand lists for this `fg` on the BASE `bg` token, not on the blend. A gradient is not measured: pass the color of its strongest point as `with` and that point's opacity as `withAlpha`. Refused, never guessed: a translucent `bg`, a `with` that is not a color blazon can read, an unknown token, `with` without `withAlpha` or the reverse, an opacity outside 0 to 1.

mcpTools.name: get_fonts
mcpTools.title: Read the brand fonts
mcpTools.description: Gets the font stylesheets and font files the brand loads, and for each font family a token names whether the brand loads it. Use it to load the same fonts as the brand instead of typing a font address. With css it also returns the @font-face rules for the font files, with base as their URL prefix. For the family a token names, use get_token.

mcpTools.name: get_logo
mcpTools.title: Read the brand logo
mcpTools.description: Gets the brand logo variants for light and dark surfaces, their files, and the rules for each logo: clear space, minimum size, lockups, and the backgrounds that forbid it. Use it before placing a logo. For the brand's other rules use get_rules.

chapters.title: Building a website from a brand

readme.quickStart:
npm install @iksnerd/blazon
npx blazon init my-brand
npx blazon dev my-brand   # the book, with live reload, at http://localhost:3000
readme.agentPrompt:
Set up a blazon brand book here. Install it with `npm install @iksnerd/blazon` (never run `npx blazon`
before that: the npm package named `blazon` is an unrelated project), then run it as `npx blazon`.
Run `blazon init brand` (add `--from <site url>` to read a site's colors, fonts and logo).
Read brand/AGENTS.md and follow it. Replace the starter's tokens, docs and assets with my brand:
<my colors, fonts and logo, or the site address>. Ask me for any color, font or license you
do not have; do not guess one. Run `blazon check brand` and fix each finding until it reports no
errors, then run `blazon build brand` and tell me what is still marked needs-review.
Then run `blazon mcp --check --brand brand`; if it reports a failed check or `registered: false`,
run the `fix` it names, and register the server with `blazon mcp --print-config --brand brand`.
